INITIAL RESPONSE:
 The correct answer is **B. Inferior vena cava**. Here's why:

* Before the stress test, the inferior vena cava (IVC) contains a low volume of blood that is well-oxygenated as it is fed by the hypoxic pulmonary veins.
* After the stress test, the IVC still contains a relatively low volume of blood as it is not until after the right side of the heart empties that blood flows retrograde from the hepatic and splenic veins to the IVC. The blood in the IVC is still relatively oxygen rich at this time.
* In contrast, the pulmonary artery and pulmonary vein will have the highest oxygen content at both time points because they contain blood that has just been oxygenated in the lungs.
* The superior vena cava and coronary sinus will have the highest oxygen content after the stress test as they now contain a volume of oxygenated blood that has been redistributed due to the body’s increased oxygen demand.
